note: Original Ontario, Simcoe and Huron line (Northern Railway of Canada from 1858/59). Opened May 16, 1853, when passenger service began between Toronto and Aurora (Machell's Corners); the source calls it the oldest operating railway line in Ontario.

Great Western Railway's Toronto branch from Hamilton along the lakeshore; the source says only that the Toronto branch opened in 1855 (no day or month). The name Hamilton and Toronto Railway for the building company was not verified in the source opened.

Grand Trunk line from Toronto west to Guelph and Sarnia. The source says the Grand Trunk built its Weston station in 1856; a second page says Brampton station opened in 1856 on this line (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brampton_GO_Station). No source found stating the exact opening date of the Toronto stretch; the whole Toronto-Sarnia line was finished November 1859.
Grand Trunk Montreal-Toronto main line; the source says the section from Montreal to Toronto opened in October 1856. The date is for the whole line, not specifically the Toronto stretch.

Credit Valley Railway main line. The source says the line opened from Parkdale station to Milton in 1877; it also gives a formal opening in September 1879 and says the connection from Parkdale into Union Station came in 1880. Doubt: 1877 is the source's year but may be early for regular service.

Toronto, Grey and Bruce narrow-gauge line via Weston and Bolton to Orangeville, opened to Orangeville in September 1871 (converted to standard gauge by 1881, CPR from 1883 per https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Weston_GO_Station). Doubt: the TG&B at first reached Weston by a third rail in the Grand Trunk track, so the separate track between West Toronto and Weston may be later; no date found for it.

Ontario and Quebec Railway Toronto-Perth line (CPR-controlled, leased to the CPR in 1884) through North Toronto; construction began 1882 and the line was completed in August 1884. The date is for the whole line, not specifically the Toronto stretch.

Inside Toronto (Leaside to Agincourt) this is the Ontario and Quebec Railway Toronto-Perth line, completed August 1884. The date is for the whole line; the present lakeshore route east of Agincourt is a later CPR line and is outside the city.

Canadian Northern's Toronto-Parry Sound line (chartered as the James Bay Railway, later Canadian Northern Ontario Railway), completed in 1906; no day or month given. The short stretch in the Don valley south of Winchester Street reused the 1892 Toronto Belt Line right-of-way (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Toronto_Belt_Line_Railway).

CPR Don Branch from Leaside down the Don valley to Union Station: opened to freight September 7, 1892, passenger trains from May 14, 1893. End of use is from a second source, a personal history site: last train was the CP Holiday Train in November 2007 (https://militarybruce.com/the-half-mile-bridge-a-silent-monument-to-the-grand-era-of-the-railways/). The track is disused, not lifted; the Province bought the branch in April 2009 (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Mills_Trail).

Bridge on the CPR Don Branch; same dates as the branch (freight September 7, 1892, passengers May 14, 1893, last train November 2007 per https://militarybruce.com/the-half-mile-bridge-a-silent-monument-to-the-grand-era-of-the-railways/). That site says the present bridge was built in the 1920s, replacing an 1891 bridge; not confirmed by a second source.

West of Bay Street only. The first train of 16 May 1853 left a depot near Bay and Front (see the STATION rows), so track ran along the waterfront from there to the line north; no source states this stretch separately. Drawn on the present corridor.

East of Bay Street. Tracks along the Esplanade: the City granted the Grand Trunk a 40-foot strip on January 21, 1856 and its east and west terminals were joined across the unfinished Esplanade in 1857. Railways had reached the waterfront earlier (Ontario, Simcoe and Huron 1853, Great Western to Queen's Wharf 1855, per https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Toronto_Union_Station_(1858)). The present raised viaduct was built from 1925 and opened to traffic on January 21, 1930.

Toronto Belt Line Railway (operated by the Grand Trunk); passenger service began July 30, 1892 and ceased November 17, 1894. end_year is the end of passenger service, not of the track: the Grand Trunk rebuilt this section (Fairbank Junction to Mount Pleasant Road) for freight in 1910, and freight east of Allen Road ended in 1970.

Toronto Belt Line Railway (operated by the Grand Trunk); passenger service began July 30, 1892 and ceased November 17, 1894. end_year is the end of passenger service, not of the track: no source found for any later use of the Moore Park ravine section, which appears to have gone out of use in 1894.

Toronto Belt Line Railway (operated by the Grand Trunk); passenger service began July 30, 1892 and ceased November 17, 1894. end_year is the end of passenger service, not of the track: if this is the section west of Allen Road (York Beltline), it carried freight from 1910 until CN sold it to the city in 1988 (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Beltline_Trail). Which section OSM means by this name was not checked.

Leaside Spur (Leaside Cutoff, Oriole Spur) between Oriole on the Bala Subdivision and Donlands on the CPR Belleville Subdivision; opened February 1, 1918, bought by the CNR the same year, abandoned by the CNR in 1999.
Trail on the roadbed of the Leaside Spur: opened February 1, 1918, abandoned by the CNR in 1999.
Station fact only, not a line. The first passenger train left Toronto in 1853 from a wooden depot near Bay and Front Streets.
Station fact only. Opened June 21, 1858, just west of the present Union Station train shed (York Street and the Esplanade per https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Esplanade_(Toronto)); demolished 1871.
Station fact only. Opened July 1, 1873 on the site of the 1858 station; replaced when the present Union Station opened in August 1927 and dismantled over the following year.

Station fact only. The Great Western built its own station at Yonge Street and the Esplanade in 1866; before that it ran from a station at Queen's Wharf (1855). No closing year sourced; the site later became the O'Keefe Centre (Meridian Hall).
Station fact only. CPR station on the North Toronto Subdivision at Yonge Street (now an LCBO store); opened for passenger service June 14, 1916, last paying passengers September 27, 1930.
